## 2. Learning metrics (analytics steward)

Report the controllable inputs and the outputs separately. Engagement numbers come last and come labelled.

**We have no real-learner data.** Nothing has been deployed with the event API in use by real learners (company/ops/deployments/ holds only its README), and EXP-002 is still "designed, not run". So recall, completion and dwell are empty, not zero. What would produce the first numbers:
- **Prediction → reveal completion and dwell:** a founder-approved deploy with real visitors. The numbers are available from the first day of traffic, but only if someone keeps the logs: `/api/events` only does `console.log` (src/app/api/events/route.ts), so without a log export there is still nothing to count. That is a logging gap to close before the deploy, not after it.
- **Revisit recall:** the first revisit is due 1 day after a lesson (`REVISIT_SCHEDULE_DAYS = [1, 3, 7, 21]` in src/kit/progress.ts), so the earliest number is deploy day + 1, from browsers that come back. EXP-002 (5 adults × 5 lessons, recall 3 days later, founder runs the sessions) gives its first result 3 days after the first session. No session is scheduled, so there is no date. Its committed prediction (recall ≥ 60%; wrong if ≤ 45%) stands as written.

Batch D's common cause, the answer in the option wording, was in all 14 lessons, which makes it a template/brief fault (W-599, W-613). Pooled: 26 of 49. |

**Logging check (Twyman), console errors.** All 9 have the same text, React's dev-mode warning "Can't perform a React state update on a component that hasn't mounted yet". All 9 fall between 17:10 and 17:58 UTC, the hour when the median passing QA run took 69 s against 9–17 s in every hour from 08 to 14 UTC. Every one passed on rerun, and the 44 qa-official runs at 18:10–18:15 all passed. So read these as the overloaded dev server (slow hydration), not 9 lesson defects. Confidence is medium: none was reproduced on a release build. If the warning shows up on a quiet server or a release build, it is a kit/lesson bug and goes to platform-engineer.
**Logging check, timeouts.** 41 of the 54 distinct failed results today were 45 s timeouts, mostly `page.goto` never reaching "load". They measure the host, not the lessons, and they are left out of the row above.

Anything that looks interesting is probably wrong (Twyman). Before explaining a move, check logging, sample ratios and novelty.

Top roles by runs: demo-builder 162 runs (16 stopped, 149k tokens/run, median 19 min), fact-checker 78 (0, 131k, 7 min), learner-evaluator 65 (5, 179k, 18 min), general-purpose 23 (1, 177k, 13 min), interaction-designer 13 (0, 111k, 9 min). The full table is in `npm run metrics -- --md`.

**Logging check first: the event log stops at 15:20 UTC.** The last `dispatch` in company/ops/events.jsonl is at 14:55 and the last `report` at 15:20. But progress.md and the build notes show about 15 more sessions running from 15:20 to 18:15: the Wave J builders for math, cs, probability, life, chemistry, geography and ai, Books, the Big Ideas pilot, the r9 revisions, the Life Hacks a11y work, fact-checkers W-639/W-655/W-657, and domain-scout. None of them are in the log. So every number in this table **leaves out the overloaded window**, and the 5% stop rate cannot answer the concurrency question on its own.

- **Roles never dispatched (49 of 90).** Part of this is the logging gap: domain-scout wrote a progress entry today and is still listed as never dispatched, and so is analytics-steward (this run). Of the rest:
  - Checks being skipped, with the work done by someone else: learning-designer (builders write recall questions themselves, e.g. ties-keep-their-order build.md, "the learning designer should review"); privacy-reviewer (the event API is due to go live; see section 2); qa-tester (8 runs, against 1,531 QA results today, almost all run by builders on their own lessons, with W-643, W-681 and W-659 still waiting for an official record). These should be dispatched, not retired.
  - Probably unneeded at this size: the ~25 strand-level category managers (cm-math-algebra, cm-physics-waves, …). Their parent cm-* wrote the Wave J strand briefs. That is a candidate for consolidation with offboarding records. Org design is not mine to decide (chief-of-staff / head-of-product).
  - Not yet needed: localization, personalization, community and R&D roles. Leave them dormant and say so.
- **Stop rate (5% overall; today 2 of 346 dispatches, both usage limits at 11:56; yesterday 30 of 130).** Usage stops are below the 10% line. **But the concurrency did hurt throughput, through the host, not the usage budget.** Today ran up to 20 agents at once (the event log's peak is 20 live, at 06:51), against the default of about 8 in operating-loop.md. The 2026-10-14 upgrade section there allows up to 30 on usage grounds. Load averages were 25–60. The evidence:
  - The median passing QA run per lesson and viewport was 9–17 s from 08 to 14 UTC and **69 s at 17 UTC** (n = 104), then 11 s at 18 UTC once load fell.
  - Builders report pages taking 20 s to 4 min, with a worst of 730 s (about 12 min; probability). A cold compile took about 35 min (life). The stock tools/reveal-fit.mjs timed out "on every attempt" (books, probability, math, ai), so builders measured with scratch copies that raise only the timeouts.
  - 48 build notes record QA run with a raised `--timeout` (240,000 to 900,000 ms, against the stock 45 s). 276 of 1,044 lesson/viewport pairs ran more than once. 41 of 54 failures were timeouts.
  - Everyone shares one dev server, :3530, so one fault takes down every agent. A syntax error in cs/nearest-town-first-detours returned HTTP 500 on every page for about 20 min.

  Net: past about 8 agents on one host, each extra builder added load more than lessons. Builder minutes went into waiting and reruns, and every measurement moved onto patched tools. I cannot give a lessons-per-hour figure, because the overloaded window is not in the event log. **Re-plan concurrency on host load, not on stop rate.** Either cap the agents sharing :3530 at about 8, or enforce the operating-loop.md dispatch rule (each parallel builder gets its own worktree, `NEXT_DIST_DIR`, `QA_PORT` and server). Today's builders did not have their own servers. Owners: chief-of-staff (dispatch), principal-engineer-ops (host capacity, ops review W-531), platform-engineer (configurable timeouts in reveal-fit and QA, unfiled).
- **Tokens per run by role.** There is no last-week baseline, because this is the first filled table, so today's figures become the baseline. Build tokens per lesson stay flat across waves (w1 24k, w2 20k, w3b+w4 21k), so there is no sign of a bloated builder brief. Watch learner-evaluator (179k/run, the highest of the frequently run roles) and the single 227k cm-course-ncm run.
- **Rework (45%).** The definition is version > 1. That counts fact-check fixes and phone-fit cuts as well as learner revisions, and lessons built today cannot have been revised yet, so the ratio will rise mechanically as they age. Do not read a trend from it until it is split by cause. The upstream signal today is r9 batch D: the answer was in the option wording in 14 of 14 Life Hacks lessons. That is a template/brief fault for cm-lifehacks (W-599, W-613), not a builder fault.
- **First-review launch rate by model (EXP-003): sonnet 67% vs opus 51%.** This looks interesting, so it gets a logging check, and it fails it. (1) Attribution: a build counts as "sonnet" only if build.md contains the text "sonnet build", and everything else, including unlabelled builds, defaults to opus. (2) Time confound: Sonnet builds are concentrated in later waves, built after the earn-the-reveal rules, and the 2026-10-13 WBR saw launch rates rise for every build after those rules. (3) "First" verdict means the alphabetically first learner file. The committed falsifier (Sonnet more than 15 points *below* Opus) has not fired. But **this is not evidence that Sonnet builds better.** A fair read needs the comparison restricted to the same waves.
- **Brief errors found by builders: 10**, counted from build notes headed 2026-10-14 (244 notes) plus board items. Each is a factual error in the brief that the builder recomputed and corrected:
  - cs: nearest-town-first-detours (nearest-first ties with 7 other orders at 56, not "the longest"; W-658); heapify-from-the-bottom ("leaves never move" is false); queue-or-stack-same-search (the stack order is wrong for that graph); kmp-never-steps-back ("never re-reads text" is false, 14 comparisons over 9 letters); clear-the-lowest-one (the stated misconception is false in decimal too); one-crowded-bucket (check line wrong in two places, also caught by the spec, W-181).
  - physics: duck-rides-the-wave (the buoy timing uses crest speed; the group speed c/2 gives about 32 s, not 16 s; W-581).
  - big-ideas: earth-history-in-a-day ("move continents" credited to 18th–19th-century geologists; continental drift is 20th-century).
  - life: stable-until-mutants-meet (1.2% at 400 generations; the re-run gives 2.9%).
  - math/NCM: broker-between-two-groups (Hana is not the best-connected person; W-187).

  Also: 1 spec error (earliest-finish-wins: "B, C, D overlap in pairs" is false) and 1 figure that could not be reproduced (new-server-moves-few-keys 19.6%). Not counted here: brief-origin errors found by fact-checkers (checking-is-not-finding c4, heat-the-ammonia-maker c2/c3). This is a grep count, so it is a lower bound. **6 of the 10 come from cs.algorithms briefs**, which is the category-manager quality signal for cm-cs / cm-cs-algorithms. Only 3 of the 10 have a board item, so the other 7 need routing to their category managers so the briefs get corrected at the source.
